# To evaluate time series models using AIC.

## Load the required packages
```{r}
library(forecast)
```


## Generate random time series data and Get the data points in form of a R vector.
```{r}
rain <- c(987,1025,978,774,1563,569,1456,789,1479,566,1563,1698)

```

## Convert it to a time series object.
```{r}
rain_ts <- ts(rain,start = c(2020,1),frequency = 12)
print(rain_ts)
```

## Timem Series Plot of the data
```{r}
plot(rain_ts, main = "Time series data")
```

## Summary of data
```{r}
summary(rain_ts)
```
## Build a model using arima()

```{r}

model <- arima(rain_ts, order = c(1,0,0))
model
```

```{r}

model2 <- arima(rain_ts, order = c(2,0,0))

model2
```
### The lower the aic term , the better the model.Hence we choose the a model with order - (1,0,0)

## Calculate the AIC values
```{r}

AIC(model)
AIC(model2)

```
### Clearly the model1 with arima parameters (1,0,0) is better then model2 as the AIC value of model 1 (179.4) is lesser then AIC of model 2 (181.2)

## Custom Dataset
### Dataset: Number of Covid-19 Vaccinated people from 15 January 2021 to March 12th 2021

## Loading the data
```{r}
library(readxl)
Production <- read_excel("C:/Users/Admin/Downloads/Dataset1.xlsx")
View(Production)
head(Production)
```

## Description of Data
```{r}
pro = subset(Production, select= -c(Year))
data= ts(pro)
head(data)
ts.plot(data)
summary(data)

```
## Build a model using arima()

```{r}
model_p1 <- arima(data, order = c(1,0,0))
model_p1
```

```{r}
model_p2 <- arima(data, order = c(1,1,0))
model_p2
```
```{r}
model_p3 <- arima(data, order = c(2,1,0))
model_p3
```
### Comparing the models, the model with the lowest AIC score wil be chosen that is model 3 with an AR(2) process and a differencing factor of 1.
